name: Brow shaping guide / stencil
lead: A brow shaping guide or stencil is a template placed over the eyebrow to outline a target shape. The user then fills the outline with pencil or powder, or uses its edge as a boundary when trimming or removing stray hairs. People use them to get brows that look even, symmetrical and defined, which frames the eyes and changes how the upper face reads.[1]

Brows are among the most mobile features of the face and are described as important for communicating emotion, which is part of why their shape is a common target for grooming.[1] Shaping is typically done by tweezing, waxing, threading or trimming, while pencils, powders and gels add fullness or definition, and cosmetic tattooing or microblading offers a longer-lasting outline.[1] A stencil sits alongside these methods as a way to repeat the same shape each time.
No published clinical studies of brow stencils were found, and the encyclopedic coverage of eyebrows describes the tools and methods generally rather than stencils specifically.

paras: People commonly shape brows with tweezers, waxing or threading, and sometimes trim them with small scissors.[1] Stencils offer a fixed outline for these steps; the template is held over the brow and the shape is traced with pencil or powder, or stray hairs outside the outline are removed.

Brow styles have changed repeatedly through history, from Japanese hikimayu practices dating to the 8th century, in which brows were shaved or plucked and painted higher on the forehead, to Elizabethan high-status women removing brows and the thin plucked brows of the 1920s and 1930s.[1]

Brow pencils, shaders and brushes define the brow or imitate hairs in sparse areas, brow gels add texture, and powders or eyeshadows in a shade near the natural hair colour give a softer fill.[1] Some people shave or wax the brows and draw them on, or have them tattooed; in the 21st century cosmetic tattooing or microblading, which places pigment in fine strokes, has become a popular way to keep a brow shape, and eyebrow transplants move follicles to bare areas.[1]
Dye is also used to darken brows, and Wikipedia notes that men in Western societies are said to pluck parts of their brows, though that statement is flagged as needing a citation.[1]
General references say tweezing and waxing can hurt for seconds or minutes, with the discomfort often lessening as people become used to it.[1] No product-specific safety data on stencils were found.

card.summary: A template that outlines a brow shape for filling or trimming; no research exists on it.
card.note: No studies found; hair removal done with it carries the usual risks of the chosen method.

quick.overview:
A brow stencil is a plastic or similar template laid over the brow to mark a shape. Users then fill in or remove hair according to the outline.

No clinical studies or detailed reference material were found.
quick.mechanism: It acts only as a visual guide; the shape change comes from pencil, powder or hair removal.
quick.risks: No product-specific safety data were found. Shaping methods such as tweezing and waxing can be briefly painful, according to general references.

angle.text: The stencil fixes a brow shape in place so both sides can be filled or trimmed to match. Users say this gives symmetrical, defined brows without freehand guesswork.
